title: Refinement comparisons intertwine strict-system projection maps
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\ge1$. For each scheme $W$ below put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$ on a fixed small representative of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\mathscr S_W$ for the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of these module sheaves, with componentwise morphisms commuting with the quotient transitions, and use its ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathscr S_W)$ [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use the simultaneous system functors $P_u=u^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$ with $P_u\dashv R_u$, unit $\eta_u$, counit $\varepsilon_u$, and exact open extension $j_!$ of that node. Write $\mu_u:P_u(F\otimes^LG)\cong P_uF\otimes^LP_uG$ for the canonical tensor comparison. Let $\pi_{u;H,Q}:R_uH\otimes^LQ\to R_u(H\otimes^LP_uQ)$ be the transpose of $(\varepsilon_{u,H}\otimes1)\mu_u$, and $\delta_{j;H,Q}:j_!H\otimes^LQ\cong j_!(H\otimes^LP_jQ)$ the canonical open tensor comparison [def-exchange-projection, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $c_i=(j_i:X\hookrightarrow\overline X_i,p_i:\overline X_i\to Y)$ for $i=1,2$ be compactifications of $f$, and let $u:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ be a proper refinement, so $uj_1=j_2$ and $p_2u=p_1$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $F_i=R_{p_i}j_{i!}$. Use the geometric proper/open mate $\gamma_u:j_{2!}\to R_uj_{1!}$, defined by open base change and clopen-component projection as in [lem-pur-system-clopen-tensor-compatibility] for the square $(k_1,i,r,p_1)=(j_1,j_2,\mathrm{id}_X,u)$. On systems whose levels have bounded cohomology with constructible pro-etale cohomology sheaves [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], it is invertible. Let $c_{p_2,u}:R_{p_1}\cong R_{p_2}R_u$ be the canonical direct-image compositor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and define
$$\theta_u=R_{p_2}(\gamma_u^{-1})c_{p_2,u}:F_1\xrightarrow{\sim}F_2,$$
the strict-system version of the specified refinement comparison [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism]. Define
$$\operatorname{PF}^{c_i}_{M,N}=R_{p_i}(\delta_{j_i;M,P_{p_i}N})\,\pi_{p_i;j_{i!}M,N}:F_iM\otimes^LN\to F_i(M\otimes^LP_fN).$$
If $M\in D(\mathscr S_X)$ and $N\in D(\mathscr S_Y)$ are normalized systems whose levels lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ and $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_n)$ respectively, meaning bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude and invertible transition-adjoint maps [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], then
$$\theta_{u,M\otimes^LP_fN}\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}_{M,N}
=\operatorname{PF}^{c_2}_{M,N}(\theta_{u,M}\otimes1_N).$$
Both sides are maps $F_1M\otimes^LN\to F_2(M\otimes^LP_fN)$ in $D(\mathscr S_Y)$ before evaluation or total inverse limit. No common cohomological or Tor bound in $n$ is required.

For identity refinements $\theta_1=1$; for composable proper refinements $u:c_1\to c_2$ and $v:c_2\to c_3$, $\theta_{vu}=\theta_v\theta_u$, with the canonical derived compositors. For any two compactifications, comparison via a common refinement is independent of that refinement; for three choices these comparisons satisfy the cocycle. These identities hold on the same levelwise bounded constructible system domain, in the derived category of systems before evaluation.

proof.text: Work in the simultaneous enhanced section models for $D(\mathscr S_W)$. The counit transpose defining $\pi_u$, the open tensor comparison $\delta_j$, and their composites are specified transformations in these models. Evaluation preserves these constructions and their composition, but is not used to detect equality of morphisms. Naturality of $\pi$ follows from its unit/counit formula and naturality of the tensor comparison; $\delta$ is the natural open-adjunction comparison. All subsequent tensor symbols denote derived tensor.

proof.text: Put $T=M\otimes^LP_fN$. At each $n$, pullback preservation gives $(P_fN)_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$, with the same Tor interval as $N_n$. Tensor preservation then gives $T_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$, with the sum of the two level-$n$ Tor intervals. The normalized-system closure lemma applies to the ring systems $B_{n,X}=f^{-1}B_{n,Y}$: the actual transition-adjoint of $P_fN$ is $f^{-1}\alpha^N_{m,n}$, and that of $T$ is the strong monoidal scalar-extension comparison followed by $\alpha^M_{m,n}\otimes\alpha^{P_fN}_{m,n}$. Both are invertible. Thus $M$ and $T$ have the domain properties needed below. All bounds here are chosen separately at each $n$. No assertion about normalization of $R_pj_!M$ is needed, since the operations and projection transformations are defined in the ambient unbounded system categories.

source.place: Clauses (i) and (ii); agent domain check combining this finite-level result with lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude and the transition-adjoint formulas of lem-pur-system-normalized-tensor-closure. There is no blueprint strict-system domain-check paragraph.

proof.text: Let $K$ be any system with bounded constructible levels, including $M$ and $T$. For each $n$, constructible origin supplies $L_n\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$ and $\nu_X^*L_n\simeq K_n$. Apply the fixed-ring proper/open calculus only with $B=A_n$, to the constant-in-the-tower-index system with value $K_n$ and identity transitions. Its finite-origin hypothesis holds with $\Lambda_m=A_n$ and $L_m=L_n$ at every auxiliary tower index $m$. Hence its evaluated refinement mate is an isomorphism, normalized as the finite proper/open comparison. Separately, the varying-ring pasting lemma with $R_n=A_n$ constructs the actual semilinear mate $\gamma_u$ and identifies its evaluation with this constant-$A_n$ mate. Evaluation detects equivalences in the semilinear section category, so $\gamma_{u,K}$ is invertible. Evaluation of $R_{p_2}(\gamma_{u,K}^{-1})c_{p_2,u}$ is exactly the finite comparison of the refinement-comparison definition, with the witness just chosen. This proves the finite normalization without asserting that derived evaluation is faithful on morphisms.

proof.text:
Apply the strict-system clopen tensor-mate identity to $(k_1,i,r,p_1)=(j_1,j_2,1_X,u)$ and $Q=P_{p_2}N$. The refinement definition supplies $uj_1=j_2$ and $p_2u=p_1$, and all schemes are separated finite-type over $k$. The compactification spaces are Noetherian: $p_i$ is proper, hence finite-type, and finite-type composition over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives this by the cited Noetherian lemma. Each inverse image of an affine chart under $j_i$ is an open subscheme of that Noetherian chart, hence quasi-compact by the cited open-subscheme lemma. Thus $j_i$ is quasi-compact. The identity-left projection is the identity under the unit identifications. Write $K_i=j_{i!}M$ and $d_i=\delta_{j_i;M,P_{p_i}N}$. After the canonical pullback identifications the cited identity is
$$\gamma_{u,T}d_2=R_u(d_1)\pi_{u;K_1,P_{p_2}N}(\gamma_{u,M}\otimes1).$$
Its source is $K_2\otimes P_{p_2}N$, and its target is $R_uj_{1!}T$. This is already an equality in the derived category of varying-coefficient systems.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), refinement square; agent specialization of lem-pur-system-clopen-tensor-compatibility

proof.text:
Use the ambient system compositor and tensor/composition coherence in setting (b) of the cited pasting lemma. For $H\in D(\mathscr S_{\overline X_1})$ and $Q\in D(\mathscr S_Y)$, put $H'=H\otimes P_{p_1}Q$. The typed projection-composition identity is
$$c_{p_2,u,H'}\pi_{p_1;H,Q}
=R_{p_2}(\pi_{u;H,P_{p_2}Q})\pi_{p_2;R_uH,Q}(c_{p_2,u,H}\otimes1_Q).$$
Indeed, transpose under $P_uP_{p_2}\dashv R_{p_2}R_u$. On both sides, the tensor/composition identity first splits the tensor pullback; the counit on its first factor is
$$P_uP_{p_2}R_{p_2}R_uH\xrightarrow{P_u\varepsilon_{p_2,R_uH}}P_uR_uH\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{u,H}}H.$$
The second factor is unchanged. The composite-adjunction counit and mate-pasting statements therefore give equal transposes, hence equal maps. This calculation takes place in the same section models.

source.place: Tags 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map) and 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); explicit agent transpose calculation using the cited system tensor/composition coherence

proof.text:
Since both refinement mates in Step 4 are invertible by Step 3, that equation gives
$$\gamma_{u,T}^{-1}R_u(d_1)\pi_{u;K_1,P_{p_2}N}
=d_2(\gamma_{u,M}^{-1}\otimes1).$$
Apply $R_{p_2}$ and precompose with $\pi_{p_2;R_uK_1,N}(c_{p_2,u,K_1}\otimes1_N)$. On the left, naturality of $c$ and Step 5 identify the result with $\theta_{u,T}R_{p_1}(d_1)\pi_{p_1;K_1,N}$. On the right use the explicit naturality equation
$$R_{p_2}(\gamma_{u,M}^{-1}\otimes1)\pi_{p_2;R_uK_1,N}
=\pi_{p_2;K_2,N}(R_{p_2}(\gamma_{u,M}^{-1})\otimes1).$$
The result is $R_{p_2}(d_2)\pi_{p_2;K_2,N}(\theta_{u,M}\otimes1_N)$. By the specified definitions these are exactly the two required projection/refinement composites, with common source $F_1M\otimes N$ and target $F_2T$.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); agent substitution of the clopen tensor identity into the typed projection-composition equation

proof.text:
Let $u:c_1\to c_2$ and $v:c_2\to c_3$. The varying-ring vertical-pasting statement gives the typed equation
$$c_{v,u,j_{1!}}\gamma_{vu}=R_v(\gamma_u)\gamma_v:j_{3!}\longrightarrow R_vR_uj_{1!}.$$
The ambient system compositors are associative, so the two maps from $R_{p_1}$ to $R_{p_3}R_vR_u$ satisfy
$$R_{p_3}(c_{v,u})c_{p_3,vu}=(c_{p_3,v}R_u)c_{p_2,u},\qquad p_2=p_3v.$$
Inverting the first equation and using the second rewrites the definition of $\theta_{vu}$ as
$$R_{p_3}(\gamma_v^{-1})\,R_{p_3}R_v(\gamma_u^{-1})\,c_{p_3,v,R_uj_{1!}}\,c_{p_2,u,j_{1!}}.$$
Here the third factor means $c_{p_3,v,R_uj_{1!}}:R_{p_2}R_uj_{1!}\to R_{p_3}R_vR_uj_{1!}$. Naturality of $c_{p_3,v}$ moves $\gamma_u^{-1}:R_uj_{1!}\to j_{2!}$ across that factor, giving precisely $\theta_v\theta_u$. Identity squares and unital compositors give $\gamma_1=1$ and $\theta_1=1$. Inverses are used on systems with bounded constructible levels, as justified in Step 3.

source.place: Tags 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose) and 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition); agent typed system compositor calculation

proof.text:
The compactification category is nonempty since $c_1$ is supplied. By compactifiable cofilteredness, for parallel refinements $a,b:d\to c$ there is a refinement $e:d'\to d$ with $ae=be$. Step 7 gives
$$\theta_a\theta_e=\theta_{ae}=\theta_{be}=\theta_b\theta_e.$$
Since $\theta_e$ is invertible on the same domain, cancellation gives $\theta_a=\theta_b$. This proves independence of the arrow, which does not follow merely from the existence of common refinement objects. The argument is an equality of strict-system natural transformations.

source.place: Tag 0ATU (lemma-compactifications-cofiltered), proof (a), condition (3), equalizer of two parallel compactification maps; explicit cancellation after Step 7

proof.text:
For a common refinement $a:d\to c_1$, $b:d\to c_2$, define $C_{12}=\theta_b\theta_a^{-1}$. Another span $a':d'\to c_1$, $b':d'\to c_2$ has a common refinement $h:e\to d$, $h':e\to d'$. By Step 8, $\theta_{ah}=\theta_{a'h'}$ and $\theta_{bh}=\theta_{b'h'}$. By Step 7,
$$\theta_b\theta_a^{-1}=\theta_{bh}\theta_{ah}^{-1}
=\theta_{b'h'}\theta_{a'h'}^{-1}=\theta_{b'}\theta_{a'}^{-1}.$$
Thus the comparison is independent both of the common object and of its chosen arrows. For three compactifications choose one common refinement, obtained by applying pairwise cofilteredness twice, with arrows $a_i$. Then
$$C_{23}C_{12}=(\theta_{a_3}\theta_{a_2}^{-1})(\theta_{a_2}\theta_{a_1}^{-1})
=\theta_{a_3}\theta_{a_1}^{-1}=C_{13}.$$
The identity, composition, independence and cocycle equations therefore hold before evaluation; their finite normalization was established in Step 3.
